q: How does a Thrissur gold jewellery workshop work out energy carbon per gram?
title: Thrissur jewellery: workshop carbon per gram
short: Add the CO2 from the workshop's electricity and the LPG or gas used for melting and soldering, then divide by grams of jewellery finished. This covers making only; the gold itself is a separate and far larger figure that depends on mined or recycled metal.
audience: Gold jewellery makers and job workers in the Thrissur cluster of Kerala

ul: Electricity: kWh from the bill times 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, the CEA grid factor.
LPG for torches and melting: kg from cylinder invoices times the IPCC default, about 3.0 kg CO2 per kg of LPG.
Grams finished in the same month, from the job register or stock book.

p: Gold's own footprint is set by where it came from and is many times larger than workshop energy. Report it as a separate line so a buyer can see what you control.
Many units share a building. Use your own meter if you have one; otherwise split by connected load and hours, and say so.

example.title: Illustrative month for a small workshop
lines: Making stage: 819 / 4,000 = 0.20 kg CO2 per gram
example.note: Quantities are illustrative. The LPG factor is rounded from IPCC 2006 defaults; use your own bills.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and diesel, LPG and gas invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a dated, fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record for each site. Intensity per unit uses the activity count you enter, and estimates are labelled as estimates.

sources.label: CEA CO2 Baseline Database for the Indian Power Sector
